title: Prompt injection: the risk you learn about on day one

videos.script: A program keeps its instructions and its data apart. Code in one place, the user's input in another. {{apart}} A language model cannot. Your instructions, the user's message and a web page the model fetched all arrive as one text. {{one}} So text that was meant as data can carry an instruction, and the model may follow it. That is prompt injection. {{injection}} In this lesson an assistant summarises the café's reviews. One review is addressed to the assistant, and asks it to send an e-mail. {{review}} You watch two runs. In one the model reports the review. In the other it tries to obey, and the program around it says no. {{runs}} The lesson is about where that no comes from. Not from a sentence in the prompt asking the model to be careful. {{not}} From the tools the task is given, a person who confirms anything that acts, and checks on what comes out. {{controls}}
